editorial.headline: Clay and Ceramic Roof Tiles, Open Nationally and Not Blocked in Bali
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 23922 covers the making of clay or ceramic roof tiles, with access across all business scales and a clear foreign-ownership ceiling nationally.
editorial.body:
KBLI 23922 is a manufacturing classification for roof tiles made from clay or ceramic. Its scope is practical and material-specific: pressed tiles, ordinary tiles, kodok-style tiles, and glazed tiles all sit inside the activity. The record is not describing retail trade, installation work, building contracting, or a broader ceramics business. It is about making the tiles themselves, from clay or ceramic inputs into finished roofing products.

That makes the code relevant for founders whose Indonesian company will operate a production activity rather than merely distribute building materials. The eligible business scales are broad: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar are all open in the record. In plain terms, the classification is not reserved only for a small workshop or only for a large industrial plant. The same activity description can support a registered operation across the full scale spectrum, provided the actual business remains within the stated roof-tile manufacturing scope.

Nationally, the PMA position is straightforward. The activity is marked TERBUKA, with a maximum foreign ownership figure of 100%. For a foreign-owned setup, that is the key national reading: the record treats the activity as open to PMA and does not state a foreign-share cap below full ownership. The cited national basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Nothing in the slim record adds a separate minimum capital number, special licence, operating threshold, or staged timeline, so those should not be inferred from this classification note.

Bali needs its own reading because the province applies a moratorium rule that blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI island-wide. For this activity, however, the Bali field is not blocked. The reason is that at Besar scale, the OSS risk level is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi, so it is not caught by the moratorium described in the record. The honest conclusion is therefore clean: a foreign investor can read KBLI 23922 as nationally open, with a 100% foreign-ownership ceiling, and the Bali record does not block PMA registration on the moratorium ground. The caution is simply editorial discipline: keep the registered activity tightly aligned with clay or ceramic roof-tile manufacturing, because the favourable reading belongs to this specific activity and its stated scope.
